purpose: Offline semantic calibration references, not production score overrides or live qualification

signedLevels: Implicit: Domain rules live only in the team's heads, or are only inferable by reading enough code and getting it wrong once.
Discoverable: Some domain documentation exists (a glossary, a rules doc) and can be found from the repo root.
Usable: Domain docs are accurate and specific enough that an agent can apply a domain rule correctly on a common task without asking.
Integrated: Domain docs are linked from the entry-point context (see context discovery) and updated as domain rules change, not just written once at project start.
Adaptive: Cases where an agent violated an undocumented domain rule get folded back into the domain docs, closing the gap for next time.
cases.reason: The supplied glossary defines concrete rules but does not show updates alongside rule changes. Static definitions and root links do not satisfy the maintained-documentation condition.

signedLevels: Implicit: Structure and constraints exist only in maintainers' heads; no docs describe them, and the codebase's actual layering has to be reverse-engineered.
Discoverable: Some architecture documentation exists (a diagram, an ADR folder, a design doc) and can be found from the repo root.
Usable: Architecture docs are accurate enough that an agent can locate the right place for a common kind of change without guessing.
Integrated: Architecture docs are linked from the entry-point context (see context discovery) and kept current alongside structural changes (e.g. ADRs added as decisions are made).
Adaptive: Cases where an agent violated an undocumented constraint get fed back into new or updated architecture docs, closing the gap.
cases.reason: The supplied architecture description and entry-point link do not establish maintenance alongside structural changes. The response itself says Integrated is unsupported.

signedLevels: Implicit: No decomposition pattern exists anywhere; every large task is tackled as one big, hard-to-review change by default.
Discoverable: Some example of decomposed work exists (a well-structured PR history, an issue broken into sub-tasks) that an agent could learn from by example.
Usable: A documented workflow or playbook explicitly models breaking a task into steps (this brain's own playbooks are an example of this for brain-maintenance tasks).
Integrated: Decomposition is connected to validation — each step in a plan has its own way to be checked before moving to the next (ties directly to verification).
Adaptive: Cases where a task was decomposed poorly (steps too large, or too tightly coupled to review independently) feed back into better decomposition guidance.
cases.reason: A small-plan expectation does not model a sequence of decomposed steps. Neither examples of decomposed work nor their absence are established.

limits: Expectations apply only to each exact paired input and rubric.
Offline review and parser compatibility do not establish v5 model compliance or scoring accuracy.
No automatic English-keyword semantic rejection or production per-concept cap is introduced.
